runs.test: tests/test_restir_di.cpp, g++ 13.3 (WSL), retro_room 96 x 64 with 96 point lights; evidence/restir-di/retro-room-96.json

r2_unbiased.observed: retro_room, 256 seeds: uniform -0.52 se, ris -0.98 se, restir -0.20 se from exact. raw-hall nave, 64 seeds: uniform +0.73, ris -1.11, restir -1.39 (bound 4)

r2b_control.observed: ris without 1/M: image mean 123.5 against exact 3.82

r3_quality.observed: single-frame relative RMSE against exact, mean of 16 seeds. retro_room: uniform 7.05, ris 2.35, restir 2.39, ratio restir/uniform 0.339 (bound 0.7). raw-hall nave: uniform 16.8, ris 3.01, restir 2.43, ratio 0.145. Every mode casts at most one shadow ray a pixel; uniform casts fewer (8,845 a frame in the hall against about 57,000) because most of its picks land on lights out of range and need no ray.

r4_bias_recorded.observed: restir_biased: retro_room -1.03 se, raw-hall -3.47 se (0.6% dark), as predicted in sign

findings: Most of the gain is resampling (ris), not spatial reuse: in the hall restir is 19% below ris; in the 96 x 64 room the two are equal within noise. The prediction (restir lower again than ris) held weakly in the hall and not in the small room.

The first spatial pass had no depth test: restir's error rose to 5.72 in the room, worse than ris (2.35), from neighbours on other surfaces. Adding the depth (10%) and normal (25 degrees) tests of Bitterli et al. 2020 fixed it before the recorded runs; at radius 3, 6, 10 and 16 the ratio was then 0.20, 0.26, 0.30 and 0.34, and the committed default (16) is the one the bounds named.
not_in_this_step: Temporal reuse; ReSTIR in the full path tracer (indirect bounces); stage 2 timing on the RTX 4090.
does_not_prove: Equal-time gains on a GPU; that the reuse gain grows at 1080p (likely, untested); quality with area or environment lights.
